voice.text: Mowgli's jungle is full of monkeys, pythons, and fig trees. [pause] It is also full of sunshine, river water, and soil. [pause] Which ones are part of the jungle's ecosystem? Tap your guess.
An <emphasis>ecosystem</emphasis> is all the living things in one place. [pause] In the jungle: tigers, deer, monkeys, bees, trees, and flowers.
<emphasis>Plus</emphasis> the nonliving things they use: sun, water, soil, and air. [pause] The deer drinks from the river. The tree feeds from the soil. [pause] Nonliving parts are on the team too.

Different places make different ecosystems. [pause] The jungle, the river, and the dry grassland have different water, different plants, and different animals. [pause] A fish belongs in the river, not the grassland.

The residents are connected in three big ways. [pause] The python <emphasis>eats</emphasis>. The deer grazes on grass — that is eating too. [pause] The bee and the flower <emphasis>help</emphasis> each other. [pause] And when the tiger and the python both want the same deer, they <emphasis>compete</emphasis>.
Put it together: living things, plus nonliving things, plus all their connections. [pause] That is an ecosystem. Mowgli's jungle is one big team.
Build the jungle ecosystem! [pause] For each card, tap: belongs in the jungle, or does not belong.
The jungle is built — living and nonliving parts together! [pause] Now, how are they connected?
How are these two connected? [pause] Tap eat, help, or compete.
You found all the connections! [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. It is not alive — but do the jungle's living things <emphasis>use</emphasis> it? Then it is part of the ecosystem.
Not quite. It is living — but is <emphasis>this</emphasis> the place it is built for? Think about heat and water.
Not quite. Nobody gets hurt here. [pause] When both sides win, that is helping.
Not quite. Big does not eat everything. [pause] Ask: do they want the same food?
Not quite. Think: who gets food, who gets help, who wants the same thing?
Yes! A living hunter of this jungle. In it goes!
Yes! Nonliving — but every plant needs it. The sun is on the team!
Yes! A living plant of the jungle. It feeds monkeys and birds.
Yes! Nonliving — but every animal drinks it. Water is part of the ecosystem!
Yes! A living resident, at home in these trees.
Yes! Nonliving — but roots and worms depend on it. Soil belongs!
Yes! A polar bear is living — but its ecosystem is icy sea, not hot jungle.
Yes! Nonliving — but every resident breathes it. Air belongs!
Yes! A cactus is living — but it is built for the dry desert, not the wet jungle.
Yes! The bee gets nectar, the flower gets its pollen carried. Both win — that is helping.
Yes! The python hunts the deer for food. That is eating.
Yes! The deer grazes on the grass. Plants can be the food — that is eating too.
Yes! The tiger does not eat the python. Both hunters want the same deer — they compete.
Yes! The monkey gets fruit, and drops seeds that grow into new trees. Both win — helping.
Yes! One meal, two eaters. They compete for it.
What is an ecosystem?
Is the river's water part of the jungle ecosystem?
A bee visits a flower. The bee gets food; the flower gets its pollen carried. What is this?
A tiger and a python both hunt the same deer. What are the tiger and python doing?
A huge elephant and a tiny squirrel live in the same jungle. Does the elephant eat the squirrel?
You know what makes an ecosystem! [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the jungle team once more.
Lesson done! Now go read about the real Indian jungle, and write two facts in your notebook.
